policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'he cometh into his own country' is a present, matching ἔρχεται; ἦλθεν would give 'he came'.
Pure word order within the infinitive phrase; 'to teach in the synagogue' is the only idiomatic English order for either reading.
Article on πολλοί; 'many hearing him' shows no article either way. The verse note 'Some ancient authorities insert the' is not mapped to this unit rather than to v005.
ASV 'the wisdom that is given unto this man' renders the demonstrative τούτῳ; αὐτῷ would give 'unto him'.
Article on δυνάμεις; 'such mighty works' shows no article either way, and the verse note about inserting 'the' is not mapped to this unit.
ASV keeps the whole clause inside the question as a participial phrase, 'such mighty works wrought by his hands'; the finite γίνονται would require a separate predication ('are wrought').
Article before Μαρίας; English proper name 'Mary' takes no article on either reading.
ASV 'and brother of James' renders either the connective καί or the postpositive δέ; the conjunction alone does not distinguish them.
Ἰωσῆτος and Ἰωσῆ are declensional variants of the same name; ASV 'Joses' renders either.
ASV 'And Jesus said unto them' renders καὶ ἔλεγεν or Ἔλεγεν δέ alike; neither the conjunction nor the verb form is distinguished.
ASV 'among his own kin' carries a possessive matching συγγενεῦσιν αὐτοῦ, parallel to 'his own country' and 'his own house'; the bare συγγενέσιν has no αὐτοῦ.
Word order only; 'do no mighty work' is the same English on either arrangement.
Imperfect against aorist; ASV 'he marvelled' is a simple past compatible with both.
ASV 'no bread, no wallet' keeps bread first, excluding RP's πήραν μὴ ἄρτον; the remaining two readings differ only in punctuation, which English does not distinguish.
ASV breaks to direct address, 'and, said he, put not on two coats', which renders the finite prohibition μὴ ἐνδύσησθε; the infinitive ἐνδύσασθαι would continue the indirect construction of v.8.
ἐάν and ἄν are equivalent in this indefinite relative clause; 'Wheresoever ye enter' renders either.
ASV 'whatsoever place shall not receive you' renders τόπος with a singular verb; RP's ὅσοι ἂν μὴ δέξωνται has no 'place' and is plural.
ASV ends the verse at 'for a testimony unto them'; the Sodom and Gomorrah sentence of RP is absent from the text.
Aorist against imperfect; ASV 'preached' is a simple past compatible with both.
Present against aorist subjunctive; 'that men should repent' renders either.
ASV text reads 'and he said' (singular ἔλεγεν) and the mapped textual note 'Some ancient authorities read they' relegates the plural ἔλεγον to the margin.
Word order plus perfect against aorist passive; ASV renders both with 'is risen' (compare v.16), so the English does not distinguish them.
ASV 'But others said' supplies an adversative that the asyndetic RP reading equally permits in context; the particle is not separately rendered.
English requires a copula in 'It is a prophet' whether or not ἐστίν stands in the Greek.
Article before the proper name Ἡρῴδης; 'Herod' takes no article in English either way.
ASV 'said' renders ἔλεγεν or εἶπεν alike, and the recitative ὅτι of RP is not rendered in English.
ASV reads simply 'he is risen', with no 'from the dead'; the other three readings all carry ἐκ νεκρῶν.
ASV text 'he was much perplexed' renders ἠπόρει, and the mapped note 'Many ancient authorities read did many things' places ἐποίει in the margin.
Aorist against imperfect; ASV 'made a supper' is compatible with both.
ASV text 'the daughter of Herodias herself' renders αὐτῆς τῆς Ἡρῳδιάδος, and the mapped note 'Some ancient authorities read his daughter Herodias' assigns αὐτοῦ to the margin.

ASV makes the pleasing the main clause, 'she pleased Herod', after the subordinate 'when ... came in and danced'; the genitive-absolute participle ἀρεσάσης would leave it subordinate with 'the king said' as the only main verb.
Word order with καί/δέ; ASV 'and the king said unto the damsel' renders either arrangement.
ASV 'And he sware unto her' has no adverbial 'much'; πολλά is unrepresented in the English.
ASV 'Whatsoever thou shalt ask of me' renders the indefinite relative under any of the three spellings, the recitative ὅτι of Treg/RP being untranslated.
ASV 'And she went out' renders καὶ ἐξελθοῦσα or Ἡ δὲ ἐξελθοῦσα alike.
Deliberative subjunctive against future; ASV 'What shall I ask?' fits both.
ASV writes 'John the Baptizer' here, its rendering of the participle βαπτίζοντος, and reserves 'the Baptist' for βαπτιστοῦ in the next verse.
εὐθύς and εὐθέως are the same adverb; ASV 'straightway' renders either.
Word order only; 'that thou forthwith give me' is the same English either way.
ASV 'them that sat at meat' renders the simplex or the compound alike; the prefix συν- has no separate English exponent here.
Word order only; 'he would not reject her' is the same English either way.
εὐθύς and εὐθέως are the same adverb; ASV 'straightway' renders either.
ASV 'commanded to bring his head' is the active infinitive ἐνέγκαι; the passive ἐνεχθῆναι would give 'commanded his head to be brought'.
ASV 'and he went and beheaded him' renders καὶ ἀπελθών or Ὁ δὲ ἀπελθών alike.
ASV 'they told him all things, whatsoever they had done' sets the relative clause directly after 'all things' with no intervening conjunction, which RP's added καί would supply.
ASV 'And he saith unto them' keeps the historic present λέγει; εἶπεν would give 'he said'.
Aorist against present imperative; ASV 'rest a while' fits both.
Word order, and a dative with or without ἐν; ASV 'in the boat to a desert place' renders either.
ASV 'many knew them' takes a plural object, excluding RP's singular αὐτόν; ἐπέγνωσαν and ἔγνωσαν are both rendered 'knew'.
ASV ends the verse at 'and outwent them'; RP's added 'and came together unto him' is absent.
ASV 'And he came forth and saw a great multitude' has a pronoun subject; RP's explicit ὁ Ἰησοῦς would give 'Jesus saw'.
Case of the pronoun after σπλαγχνίζομαι ἐπί; 'he had compassion on them' renders either.
ASV 'came unto him, and said' is a past tense; the historic present λέγουσιν is elsewhere kept as 'they say' in this chapter (v.37, v.38).
ASV 'buy themselves somewhat to eat' ends the verse; RP's 'bread; for they have nothing to eat' is absent.
Future against aorist subjunctive in the second verb; ASV 'and give them to eat?' renders either.
Word order only; 'How many loaves have ye?' is the same English either way.
English requires a conjunction in 'go and see' whether the Greek is asyndetic or has καί.
ASV 'commanded them that all should sit down' leaves the voice of the infinitive open; both the active ἀνακλῖναι and the passive ἀνακλιθῆναι yield this English.
κατά and ἀνά are both distributive here; ASV 'by hundreds' renders either.
κατά and ἀνά are both distributive here; ASV 'by fifties' renders either.
ASV reads 'he gave to the disciples', without a possessive; αὐτοῦ would give 'his disciples' as in v.45.
Present against aorist subjunctive of the same verb; 'to set before them' renders either.

ASV 'they took up broken pieces, twelve basketfuls' makes 'broken pieces' the object (accusative κλάσματα) with 'basketfuls' in apposition; the Treg and RP readings have genitive κλασμάτων filling accusative baskets, i.e. 'twelve baskets full of broken pieces'.
ASV 'they that ate the loaves' renders τοὺς ἄρτους, which the omitting reading lacks.
εὐθύς and εὐθέως are the same adverb; ASV 'straightway' renders either.
ASV 'to go before him unto the other side to Bethsaida' renders εἰς τὸ πέραν, which the omitting reading lacks.
ASV 'while he himself sendeth the multitude away' is a present indicative matching ἀπολύει; the subjunctive ἀπολύσῃ after ἕως would give 'until he should send away'.
ASV opens with the participle, 'And seeing them distressed in rowing'; the finite εἶδεν would give 'And he saw them'.
ASV runs 'contrary unto them, about the fourth watch' with no conjunction; RP's added καί would give 'and about the fourth watch'.
Word order only; 'him walking on the sea' is the same English either way.
ASV 'supposed that it was a ghost' renders the ὅτι clause with a finite verb; the accusative-infinitive φάντασμα εἶναι would give 'supposed it to be a ghost'.
ASV 'But he straightway spake with them' renders the adversative ὁ δέ with an expressed subject; both other readings begin with καί and no ὁ δέ.
ASV has the single intensifier 'sore amazed', which λίαν alone supplies; whether ἐκ περισσοῦ stood beside it is not shown in the English.
ASV ends the verse at 'sore amazed in themselves'; RP's added 'and wondered' is absent.
ASV 'but their heart was hardened' is adversative ἀλλά; RP's ἦν γάρ would give a causal 'for their heart was hardened'.
ASV 'they came to the land unto Gennesaret' has a separate preposition before the place name, rendering εἰς Γεννησαρέτ; the Treg/RP order makes Gennesaret an attribute of 'the land'.
εὐθύς and εὐθέως are the same adverb; ASV 'straightway' renders either.
ASV 'and ran round about that whole region, and began to carry' is a finite verb joined by 'and', matching περιέδραμον ... καί, and 'region' renders χώραν rather than RP's participle with περίχωρον.
ASV 'where they heard he was' has no 'there'; the added ἐκεῖ would give 'that he was there'.
ASV repeats the preposition, 'into villages, or into cities, or into the country', rendering εἰς before each noun; RP has the bare nouns.
ἐτίθεσαν and ἐτίθουν are alternative imperfect forms of the same verb; ASV 'they laid' renders either.
Aorist against imperfect; ASV 'as many as touched him' fits both.
